# SATA cap — uncapped vs capped replays (Strategy Logic V2)

*Generated by `scripts/eval_sata_cap.py` · data through **2026-10-10** · walk-forward gated replay, V2 with the production cluster rules, 3 optimiser seeds (7, 11, 23; 7 = production) · cells are **total return / max drawdown / Sharpe**.*

## Question

Whatever the signals leave undeployed used to sit entirely in **SATA** (Strive's variable-rate preferred: ~13 % coupon, but a preferred's price can fall) — up to 84 % of the book in the replay and 40 % in the published book at the time. What does it cost to **limit SATA to 30 % of the book and hold any excess in cash at 0 %**?

## The rule

`overall_core.SATA_CAP = 0.3` (`sata_cap_for(version)`; V2 only, **both profiles**). The idle remainder splits (`split_idle`): SATA up to the cap, the excess in cash. SATA is the allocator's residual, so **no sleeve weight changes** — only where the idle capital sits, and so how much of it earns the coupon. It is applied everywhere the book is built or replayed: the live gate (`sata` / `cash` / `idle`), the closed-market freeze, the historical book, the walk-forward replay and Combined splice (`cash` series), the P&L section's attribution, trade log and realized-P&L maths (cash earns 0 %), the costs/taxes simulator (a separate 0 %-yield cash balance), the as-published replay (books are stamped with `sata_cap`; older books are unchanged), the health tracker and the published books: the **paper** book still holds all idle as cash, the **live** book parks `min(idle, cap)` in SATA and the excess in `cash_weight`. V1 has no cap; the Combined view applies it from the 2026-10-09 cut-over.

## Reading it

* The cost is the lost coupon on the cash leg — about a 13 %/yr yield on an average 4 % of the book (24 % of days above the cap), concentrated in 2021–25 when the book was often mostly idle; recent windows lose only 1–2 points.
* Max drawdown is unchanged on the full replay and 0.1–0.2 pt deeper in recent windows (losing the carry matters slightly more in a drawdown); Sharpe moves by 0.01–0.03.
* Cost rises gradually as the cap tightens (sensitivity line above).
* **What the back-test cannot show:** it prices SATA at a steady coupon with no price risk. The cap exists to bound that exposure, so the return cost above is the premium for an insurance whose payoff the replay does not model. Cash earns 0 % here by decision (a money-market yield would shrink the cost).
* The optimiser that fits the quarterly anchors still assumes idle capital earns the SATA coupon (`_combine`), so anchors and the fixed-weight 'optimal blend' statistics ignore the cap; the published walk-forward replay, the live book and every P&L figure apply it.

## Invariants checked on every run

Sleeve weights identical capped vs uncapped · weights + SATA + cash = 100 % on every day · SATA never above the cap · the real capped replay equals the one derived from the uncapped replay (return gap = coupon on the cash leg, business days only). **PASS**.
